'''Al-Farouq Ajadi Aminu''' {{Audio|LL-Q33578 (ibo)-Obefelix-Al-Farouq Aminu.wav|Listen|help=no}}(born September 21, 1990) is a Nigerian-American former professional [[basketball]] player who played eleven seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He has also represented the [[Nigeria national basketball team]] internationally. Aminu was selected by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the [[2010 NBA draft]] with the eighth overall pick, and has played for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Portland Trail Blazers]], [[Orlando Magic]], and [[Chicago Bulls]].

==High school career==
Aminu went to [[Norcross High School]] and was ranked as one of the top college recruits in the nation from the class of 2008. He was ranked #7 in the nation by [[Rivals.com]] and #13 by Scout.com.<ref>[http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&pid=88&yr=2008 Scout.com College Football Team Recruiting Prospects]</ref>

Aminu transferred to Norcross between his freshman and sophomore years from [[Wesleyan School]], but was ruled ineligible and had to play on Norcross' [[Junior varsity team|JV]] team his sophomore year.<ref>[https://gtsports.blogspot.com/2005/12/hoops-al-farouq-aminu-ruled-ineligible.html Hoops – Al-Farouq Aminu ruled Ineligible]. Gtsports.blogspot.com (December 7, 2005). Retrieved on December 2, 2015.</ref> In his junior year, Aminu and teammate [[Gani Lawal]] led Norcross to a 30–3 record and a #12 national seed. Aminu averaged 13.7 points and 9.5 rebounds per game in his junior year. He led Norcross to back to back Georgia 5A state titles in 2007 and 2008. He averaged 23.1 points and 11.2 rebounds a game as a senior. Norcross finished 29–2 and ranked #6 in 2008. Aminu was a member of the 2008 [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American Team]] and played in the Jordan Brand Classic where he had 12 points and 13 rebounds.<ref>[http://blog.newrecruitsports.com/?p=3 Jordan Brand Classic Stats] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080928043546/http://blog.newrecruitsports.com/?p=3 |date=September 28, 2008 }}. Blog.newrecruitsports.com (July 22, 2002). Retrieved on December 2, 2015.</ref>

==College career==
Aminu committed to Wake Forest in July 2007 and in November 2007 Aminu signed a [[Letter of Intent]] to play basketball at [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]]. He chose Wake Forest over [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]].

As a freshman during the 2008–09 season, he was a unanimous selection for the ACC All-Freshman Team.  Aminu posted 10 double-doubles on the year, including five in conference action. He led all freshmen and ranked sixth in the ACC with 8.3 rebounds per game. Aminu was also second among all league rookies with 13.0 points per contest.

==Professional career==

===Los Angeles Clippers (2010–2011)===
On April 1, 2010, Aminu hired an agent and declared for the [[2010 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Al-Farouq Aminu Declares for NBA Draft|url=http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/040110aaa.html|work=WakeForestSports.com|date=April 1, 2010|access-date=December 2, 2015|archive-date=December 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208050409/http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/040110aaa.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was selected with the eighth overall pick by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. In just his eighth game for the Clippers on November 9, 2010, he had a season-best game with 20 points (a career-high until March 31, 2016) and 8 rebounds against the New Orleans Hornets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets extend franchise-best start after pasting Clippers|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=301109003|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101112112716/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=301109003|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 12, 2010|work=ESPN.go.com|date=November 9, 2010|access-date=December 2, 2015}}</ref>

===New Orleans Hornets/Pelicans (2011–2014)===
[[File:20140101 Al-Farouq Aminu (1).JPG|Aminu with the Pelicans in 2014|right|thumb|upright]]
On December 14, 2011, the Clippers traded Aminu, [[Chris Kaman]], [[Eric Gordon]] and a 2012 first-round pick (previously acquired from the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]) to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] in exchange for [[Chris Paul]] and two future second-round picks.<ref>{{cite news|title=Hornets acquire Gordon, Aminu, Kaman and first-round pick|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/hornets_clippers_trade_2011_12_14.html|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=December 14, 2011|access-date=December 15, 2011}}</ref>

In the final game of the [[2012–13 NBA season|2012–13 regular season]] on April 17, Aminu recorded 16 points and a career-high 20 rebounds in an 87–99 loss to the Dallas Mavericks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mavs avoid first losing season since 1999–2000 with win over Hornets|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/id/400278944/gameId/400278944/new-orleans-hornets-vs-dallas-mavericks|work=ESPN.go.com|date=April 17, 2013|access-date=December 2, 2015}}</ref> The next day, the Hornets changed their name to the Pelicans.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets officially become Pelicans|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/9187070/new-orleans-hornets-announce-name-change-pelicans-official|work=ESPN.go.com|date=April 18, 2013|access-date=December 2, 2015}}</ref>

On December 4, 2013, against the Dallas Mavericks once again, Aminu tied his career-best game with 16 points and 20 rebounds in a 97–100 loss.<ref>{{cite web|title=Notebook: Mavericks 100, Pelicans 97|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131204/DALNOP/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=December 4, 2013|access-date=December 2, 2015}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2014–2015)===
On July 29, 2014, Aminu signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Adam|last=Wermuth|title=Mavericks sign free agent Al-Farouq Aminu|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-free-agent-al-farouq-aminu/|work=Mavs.com|date=July 29, 2014|access-date=July 29, 2014}}</ref> On February 20, 2015, he had a season-best game with 17 points and 12 rebounds in a 111–100 win over the Houston Rockets.<ref>{{cite news|title=Harris, Aminu lead as balanced Mavs hold off Rockets 111–100|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150220/HOUDAL/gameinfo.html?ls=slt|work=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2015|access-date=December 2, 2015}}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2015–2019)===
On July 9, 2015, Aminu signed a four-year, $30 million contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Forward Al-Farouq Aminu|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-forward-al-farouq-aminu|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2015|access-date=July 13, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Al-Farouq Aminu, Blazers agree to 4-year, $30M deal, source says|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13178619/al-farouq-aminu-portland-trail-blazers-agree-terms-4-year-30-million-deal/|work=ESPN.com|date=July 1, 2015|access-date=July 1, 2015}}</ref> On August 1, 2015, he played for Team Africa at the [[NBA Africa Game 2015|2015 NBA Africa exhibition game]]. He made his debut for the Trail Blazers in the team's season opener against the New Orleans Pelicans on October 28, recording 9 points and 8 rebounds in a 112–94 win.<ref>{{cite web|title=McCollum scores 37 as Blazers down Pelicans 112–94|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/NOPPOR/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180507024227/http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/NOPPOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=May 7, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 26, 2016, Aminu matched his career high with 20 points and grabbed eight rebounds in a 108–105 win over the Philadelphia 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|title=McCollum helps Blazers escape with 108–105 win over 76ers|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160326/PHIPOR/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=March 26, 2016|access-date=March 27, 2016}}</ref> He set a new career high five days later, scoring 28 points while hitting a career-high six three-pointers in a 116–109 win over the Boston Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|title=Aminu leads Trail Blazers to 116–109 win over Celtics|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160331/BOSPOR/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=March 31, 2016|access-date=April 1, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190104215146/http://www.nba.com/games/20160331/BOSPOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 4, 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> On April 6, he scored 27 points in a 120–115 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], helping the Trail Blazers clinch a postseason berth.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers defeat Thunder 120–115, clinch playoff berth|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160406/OKCPOR/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=April 6, 2016|access-date=April 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160408140231/http://www.nba.com/games/20160406/OKCPOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 8, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Trail Blazers finished the regular season as the fifth seed in the Western Conference with a 44–38 record. In the first round of the playoffs, the Trail Blazers faced the fourth-seeded Los Angeles Clippers, and in a Game 4 win on April 25, Aminu recorded a career-high 30 points and 10 rebounds, helping the team tie the series at 2–2.<ref>{{cite web|title=Paul leaves with broken hand, Blazers beat Clippers 98–84|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160425/LACPOR/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=April 25, 2016|access-date=April 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160426052937/http://www.nba.com/games/20160425/LACPOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 26, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Trail Blazers went on to win the series 4–2 and advanced to the second round where they faced the Golden State Warriors. In Game 3 of the series, Aminu recorded 23 points and 10 rebounds to help the Trail Blazers win 120–108, cutting the Warriors' advantage in the series to 2–1.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lillard has 40, Blazers cut Warriors' advantage to 2–1|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160507/GSWPOR/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=May 7, 2016|access-date=May 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180228014751/http://www.nba.com/games/20160507/GSWPOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 28, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Trail Blazers went on to lose the series to the Warriors in five games.

After starting in the Trail Blazers' first eight games of the 2016–17 season, Aminu was ruled out for a number of weeks with a calf injury on November 11, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|first=Casey|last=Holdahl|title=AMINU OUT AT LEAST 'A COUPLE WEEKS' WITH LEFT CALF INJURY|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/forwardcenter/aminu-out-least-couple-weeks-left-calf-injury|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=November 11, 2016|access-date=November 12, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Portland Trail Blazers forward Al-Farouq Aminu out for a "couple" of weeks|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2016/11/11/portland-trail-blazers-forward-al-farouq-aminu-out-couple-weeks|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=November 11, 2016|access-date=November 12, 2016}}</ref> He returned to action on December 5 after missing 13 games and had three points in 17 minutes against the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Balanced Blazers beat Bulls 112–110 for 3rd straight win|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899750|work=ESPN.com|date=December 5, 2016|access-date=December 6, 2016}}</ref> He later missed four games in mid-December with a sore back.<ref>{{cite web|title=Barnes scores 28 and Mavericks hold off Trail Blazers, 96–95|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899878|work=ESPN.com|date=December 21, 2016|access-date=December 22, 2016}}</ref> On February 9, 2017, he scored a season-high 26 points in a 120–111 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Thomas has 34 and Celtics beat Blazers 120–111|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900203|work=ESPN.com|date=February 9, 2017|access-date=February 10, 2017}}</ref>

Aminu missed 13 games with a right ankle injury during November 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Middleton has 26 and Milwaukee beats the Blazers 103-91|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975067|work=ESPN.com|date=November 30, 2017|access-date=December 1, 2017}}</ref> On January 1, 2018, he scored a season-high 24 points in a 124–120 overtime win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|title=McCollum scores 32, leads Blazers over Bulls 124-120 in OT|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975293|work=ESPN.com|date=January 1, 2018|access-date=January 1, 2018}}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2019–2021)===
On July 6, 2019, Aminu signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Al-Farouq Aminu|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/magic-sign-al-farouq-aminu-20190706|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2019|access-date=July 6, 2019}}</ref> On December 1, 2019, the [[Orlando Magic]] announced that Aminu suffered a  torn meniscus in his right knee and would be out indefinitely.<ref>{{cite web|first=John|last=Denton|title=Aminu Out Indefinitely With Torn Meniscus|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/aminu-out-indefinitely-torn-meniscus-20191201|date=December 1, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 1, 2019}}</ref>

=== Chicago Bulls (2021) ===
On March 25, 2021, Aminu and [[Nikola Vučević]] were traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for [[Wendell Carter Jr.]], [[Otto Porter Jr.]] and two future first-round picks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bulls acquire All-Star Nikola Vucevic and Al-Farouq Aminu in trade with Magic|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-acquire-all-star-nikola-vucevic-and-al-farouq-aminu-trade-magic|work=NBA.com|date=March 25, 2021|access-date=March 25, 2021}}</ref>

On August 11, 2021, Aminu, [[Thaddeus Young]], and several draft picks were traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in exchange for [[DeMar DeRozan]].<ref>{{cite web|title=SAN ANTONIO COMPLETES TRADE WITH CHICAGO|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/san-antonio-completes-trade-chicago|work=NBA.com|date=August 11, 2021|access-date=August 11, 2021}}</ref> On October 18, Aminu was waived by the Spurs after appearing in one pre-season game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Spurs waive Al-Farouq Aminu|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-waive-al-farouq-aminu|website=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2021|access-date=October 18, 2021}}</ref> On December 25, he was signed to a 10-day contract by the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Boston Celtics|number=1474777910292754432|title=We have signed 10-year NBA veteran Al-Farouq Aminu and center Norvel Pelle to 10-day contracts.|user=celtics|date=December 25, 2021|access-date=December 26, 2021}}</ref> However, he never played a game in Boston.

==International career==
Aminu represents the [[Nigeria national basketball team|Nigerian national basketball team]]. He competed at the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men|2012 Summer Olympics]]. On August 30, 2015, Aminu with the [[D'Tigers]] of Nigeria won the [[2015 FIBA Africa Championship]] (AfroBasket) in Tunisia by defeating Angola 74–65.<ref>{{cite web|title = Nigeria defeats Angola to win first-ever FIBA African Championship title in historic Afrobasket 2015 finals|url = http://www.basketballwithinborders.com/news/nigeria-defeats-angola-to-win-first-ever-fiba-african-championship-title-in-historic-afrobasket-2015-finals/|website = Basketball|access-date = September 16, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150918185434/http://www.basketballwithinborders.com/news/nigeria-defeats-angola-to-win-first-ever-fiba-african-championship-title-in-historic-afrobasket-2015-finals/|archive-date = September 18, 2015|url-status = dead|df = mdy-all}}</ref> He was also named in the All-Star Five of the 2015 Afrobasket.<ref>{{cite web|title = Chamberlain Oguchi, Al-Farouq Aminu voted into Afrobasket 2015 All-Star Team|url = http://www.basketballwithinborders.com/news/chamberlain-oguchi-al-farouq-aminu-voted-into-afrobasket-2015-all-star-team/|website = Basketball|access-date = September 16, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150907142730/http://www.basketballwithinborders.com/news/chamberlain-oguchi-al-farouq-aminu-voted-into-afrobasket-2015-all-star-team/|archive-date = September 7, 2015|url-status = dead|df = mdy-all}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Al-Farouq Aminu has one daughter with ex-wife. He is the child of a [[Yoruba people|Yoruba]] father from Nigeria and an [[African American]] mother from New York. Aminu is descended from a line of Nigerian kings.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/portland-trail-blazers/al-farouq-aminu-and-wife-welcome-baby-girl-emanah|title=Al-Farouq Aminu and wife (at the time) welcome baby girl Emanah|access-date=March 29, 2018|archive-date=March 30, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180330012824/http://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/portland-trail-blazers/al-farouq-aminu-and-wife-welcome-baby-girl-emanah|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is a [[Muslim]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Freeman|first1=Joe|title=Trail Blazers' Al-Farouq Aminu savoring South African visit, taking part in 1st NBA Africa Game|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2015/07/trail_blazers_al-farouq_aminu.html|access-date=December 17, 2015|work=OregonLive.com|publisher=[[The Oregonian]]|date=July 30, 2015}}</ref>

His name translates to "the chief has arrived", leading to the nickname "The Chief."<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2007/highschool/12/05/al.farouq/ |title=Hail to the Chief: Norcross' Aminu Seeks Ascension to Basketball Royalty |last=O'Neill |first=Lucas |date=December 5, 2007 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |access-date=November 12, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090323084213/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2007/highschool/12/05/al.farouq/ |archive-date=March 23, 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> His brother, [[Alade Aminu]], is also a professional basketball forward.<ref>[http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/aminu_alfarouq00.html Al-Farouq Aminu Bio] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120820035129/http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/aminu_alfarouq00.html |date=August 20, 2012 }}. Wakeforestsports.com. Retrieved on December 2, 2015.</ref> Aminu and his wife's foundation, Aminu Good Works Foundation, organizes a yearly basketball camp in [[Nigeria]] since 2016. The camp takes place in [[Ibadan]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aminugoodworks.org/camp-nigeria/.|title=Aminu Good Works Foundation | Camp Nigeria}}</ref>
